A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MAMUT framework and generated datasets. The main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial additions in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset-generation statistics in Table 5 and empirical analysis of falsification strategies and symbol substitutions in Appendix B.3 and Figure 5.

after.justification: v2 retains those analyses and adds original model-training and retrieval results in Section 7, with ablations and further evaluations in Appendix C.

M1.justification: EquVG and FalseVG remain substantively unchanged, but Appendix C.1 introduces a substantial model-training extension: mixed MLM/NSP training, mathematics-aware masking for MT, and 300 additional mathematical tokens for BERT. These implemented training components go beyond v1's suggestions of possible dataset uses.

E1.justification: Using the retained MF, MT, NMF and MFR datasets, v2 adds actual training on masked-token and formula-pair tasks and evaluation of name-to-formula and formula-to-formula retrieval. v1 reports dataset generation and corpus analysis, with these learning applications only proposed. The source corpora and 71-identity collection remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v1 contains no model-baseline experiment. v2 evaluates BERT, MathBERT from Shen et al. (2021), and MPBERT against MAMUT-pretrained variants in Table 6, with checkpoints identified in Table 16. Table 21 additionally compares MPBERT variants using random or fixed negative examples.

E3.justification: v2 introduces retrieval protocols with 250 positive examples per identity, ten times as many negatives, ten-epoch fine-tuning, validation-F1 model selection, and classification and ranking metrics. It adds MLM-only pretraining controls and an NMF-Split evaluation using 49/11/11 training/validation/test identities with a frozen encoder. These are new experimental designs, not revisions to v1 model experiments.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained NMF generation analysis, Appendix C.4 adds evaluations by falsification count, substitution type, text versus formula input, and mathematical identity. It also tests challenging versus random negatives, changing versus fixed negatives, and generalization across identities excluded from fine-tuning.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports averaging five fine-tuning runs with different seeds and using different identity partitions across the five NMF-Split runs. This adds repeated-run reporting, but no standard deviations, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: The original dataset counts and Figure 5 findings are retained, while extensive model results are added. In v2 Table 6, MAMUT-MPBERT-MLM achieves NMF-FT/MFR-FT F1 scores of 87.6/80.6, compared with MPBERT's 79.9/74.0. Table 21 reports NMF-FT F1 of 79.9 with changing challenging negatives, 24.6 with random negatives and 74.4 with fixed challenging negatives. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v1 scores.

T1.justification: No substantive theorem, proof, formal assumption or derivation is added or revised. The alpha-conversion connection is conceptual explanation, and Appendix C.3 supplies standard evaluation-metric formulas rather than new theoretical results.

C1.justification: v1 principally claims a framework and four datasets suitable for mathematical language-model training. v2 adds claims of state-of-the-art mathematical retrieval performance and demonstrated benefits even for previously mathematically pretrained BERT models, alongside pretrained-model releases.

C2.justification: Sections 7–9 and Appendix C add interpretations of complementary pretraining benefits and challenging-negative effects, while acknowledging the advantage of task-related pretraining. Beyond v1's parsing caveats, v2 discusses unsupported notations, LaTeX-only applicability, possible incorrect falsifications and the need for systematic output-error analysis.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds software versions, hyperparameters, eight-A100 hardware, training-time estimates, checkpoint identifiers, and training/evaluation code locations. Appendix B.1 newly specifies SymPy filtering calls. An MT upvote criterion is also newly documented, although Sections 6 and 8.2 inconsistently apply it to answers versus questions; the PDFs do not establish that the existing datasets were regenerated.

R1.justification: The related-work narrative largely remains intact. v2 adds Shen et al.'s distinct MathBERT work while retaining Peng et al., connects substitution to alpha-conversion through Nederpelt and Geuvers, and adds supporting training and retrieval references. Section 8 further explains how notation diversity complements existing datasets' problem diversity.

P1.justification: Existing sections retain their order and mostly their wording, with localized copyediting, acronym expansions, explanatory additions and publication-header updates. The new material receives separate Experiments, Discussion, Limitations and Appendix C sections; the retained narrative is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 adds results and supporting tables, pretraining and tokenization diagrams, and a per-identity performance plot (Table 6, Tables 16–22 and Figures 6–8). Existing workflow diagrams gain icons and colored symbol highlighting. Earlier example tables and Figure 5 are retained, with renumbering and relocation distinguished from new displays.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's lack of downstream validation through model comparisons, MLM-only controls and challenging-negative ablations, while adding reproducibility information and explicit limitations. Evidence remains confined to generated retrieval tasks, and reporting defects remain: Table 20's MathBERT difference is inconsistent with its displayed accuracies, and Figure 8 retains an unfinished caption. These defects limit confidence in particular details but do not outweigh the substantial gain in empirical support.
